text:
A few years ago, if someone asked me where the future of finance was heading, I probably would’ve picked a side.

Today, I wouldn’t.

What changed wasn’t the technology.

It was my perspective.

I’ve watched people make great returns in crypto while still keeping most of their wealth in traditional investments.

I’ve watched institutions that once ignored blockchain start building products around it.

I’ve also watched crypto evolve from “just Bitcoin” into an ecosystem of payments, stablecoins, tokenized assets, AI infrastructure, DeFi, and real-world asset tokenization.

That made me realize something.

We’ve been asking the wrong question all along.

It’s never been:

Which one wins?

The real question is:

What does each system do better than the other?

If I want exposure to some of the world’s biggest companies, I still look at traditional markets.

If I want an open financial network that never closes, settles globally, and gives anyone access with an internet connection, that’s where crypto shines.

They’re solving different problems.

And that’s exactly why they fit together.

Think about what’s happening today.

Stablecoins are connecting crypto with global payments.

Tokenized assets are bringing real-world markets onto blockchains.

Banks are experimenting with digital assets.

Asset managers are offering crypto investment products.

Blockchain is quietly becoming part of financial infrastructure instead of sitting outside it.

That’s not disruption for the sake of disruption.

That’s evolution.

The people who keep treating this as a competition might miss the bigger picture.

Because while everyone debates TradFi vs. Crypto, the industry is already moving toward TradFi with Crypto.

To me, the biggest edge over the next decade won’t come from being loyal to one ecosystem.

It will come from understanding how both fit into a changing financial landscape.

The future isn’t black or white.

It’s a blend of proven systems and new technology.

And honestly, that’s a much more interesting future than either side could build on its own.

Down 2.2% overnight to $62K, but only because equities dumped. $6.2B came out of SPY and QQQ ETFs in a single day. Bitcoin just got dragged along.

Look under the hood: funding is basically zero, open interest flat, ETF flows literally $0.

No leverage flush. No short attack. No forced sellers anywhere.

Cascades need fuel. Drops without fuel drift, exhaust, and reverse. They don't accelerate.

Last time the derivatives looked this clean was early 2023. That preceded one of the best runs of the cycle.

Imported weakness, native strength. What's your read?

text:
in 2020, with my previous startup, i was leading the launch of a debit card for the crypto economy.

it failed.

the problem was real.

we were hosting hundreds of retail miners earning btc, but their everyday expenses still wanted dollars.

equipment. rent. payroll. bills. life.

crypto was becoming income.

but it still wasn’t easy to spend.

back then, the rails were too early.
regulation was not friendly.
crypto cards were barely real.
bitcoin credit was not even in the conversation.

so we stopped.

but the problem kept showing up.

then in 2024, the signals changed.

the market got louder. the rails got better. bitcoin finance started moving. crypto cards became real.

lesson:

sometimes you are not wrong.

sometimes the world just has not caught up to the problem yet.
